headline_cluster.headline: יותר מחצי מהמשברים הבנקאיים בעולם החלו כך. מה זה אומר על ישראל?

primary_source_search_status: found_snippets_only: article body unreachable (EGRESS_BLOCKED + premium paywall). Search index gives the article's on-site title 'זהו המנגנון שהופך בועת נדל"ן למשבר של ממש, וחודר לכיס של הציבור - ושל המשקיעים' (TheMarker magazine, 2026-10-05) and a snippet that 'more than half of banking crises in the world began with fluctuations in housing prices' plus a 2008 US-mortgage-market example; the outlet's named source is NOT visible in any snippet. All primary hosts tried (imf.org, federalreserve.gov, ideas.repec.org, rba.gov.au, corpgov.law.harvard.edu) were EGRESS_BLOCKED; figure confirmed via consistent search-index snippets of imf.org pages only.

claims.claim: More than half of the world's banking crises began 'this way' (per search snippet of the article: with fluctuations/booms-busts in housing prices)
claims.verified_figure: IMF (Crowe, Dell'Ariccia, Igan & Rabanal 2011; IMF blog 2014): more than two-thirds of the ~46-50 recent systemic banking crises for which house-price data exist were PRECEDED by house-price boom-bust patterns. Seen via imf.org search snippets only.
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: 'more than half' of banking crises in the world began with fluctuations in housing prices; 2008 crisis stemmed from the US mortgage-market collapse
claims.note: Judging the headline + search snippet only (body_ok 0; TheMarker's named source not visible). 'More than half' is directionally consistent with - and more conservative than - the best-known primary figure (>2/3), so no inflation of magnitude. Marked imprecise because (a) the headline's 'this way' leaves the mechanism undefined (resolved only by the snippet as housing prices); (b) the denominator 'the world's banking crises' generalizes a subset - systemic crises with available house-price data, skewed to advanced economies - to all banking crises; (c) the source reports a temporal precedence ('preceded by'), not that crises 'began' from housing, i.e. correlation rendered as origin. If the body cites a different study with a genuine 'more than half' figure, this verdict should be revisited.
